'''Sylvia Margaret Wiegand''' (born March 8, 1945) is an American mathematician.<ref name="agnesscott1">{{cite web|url=http://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/wiegand.htm |title=Sylvia Wiegand |publisher=Agnesscott.edu |date=1945-03-08 |accessdate=2012-10-31}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Wiegand was born in [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]]. She is the daughter of mathematician [[Laurence Chisholm Young]] and through him the granddaughter of mathematicians [[Grace Chisholm Young]] and [[William Henry Young]].<ref name="Sylvia Wiegand">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/wiegand.htm|title=Sylvia Wiegand|website=www.agnesscott.edu|access-date=2018-10-06}}</ref> Her family moved to Wisconsin in 1949, and she graduated from [[Bryn Mawr College]] in 1966 after three years of study.<ref name="agnesscott1"/> In 1971, Wiegand earned her Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.<ref name="autogenerated2">{{MathGenealogy|9211}}</ref> Her dissertation was titled ''Galois Theory of Essential Expansions of Modules and Vanishing Tensor Powers.''<ref name="autogenerated2"/>

== Career ==
In 1987, she was named full professor at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]]; at the time Wiegand was the only female professor in the department.<ref name="agnesscott1" />  In 1988, Sylvia headed a search committee for two new jobs in the math department, for which two women were hired, although one stayed only a year and another left after four years.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web |url=http://www.aacu.org/ocww/volume32_3/feature.cfm?section=1 |title=OCWW &#124; Vol 32, Issue 3-4 &#124; Features |publisher=Aacu.org |date= |access-date=2012-10-31 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031110164028/http://www.aacu.org/OCWW/volume32_3/feature.cfm?section=1 |archive-date=2003-11-10 }}</ref>  In 1996, Sylvia and her husband, [[Roger Wiegand]], established a fellowship for graduate student research at the university in honor of Sylvia's grandparents.<ref>{{cite web|author=PO BOX 880130 |url=http://www.math.unl.edu/department/awards/graduate/#young |title=UNL &#124; Arts & Sciences &#124; Math &#124; Department &#124; Awards &#124; Graduate Student Awards |publisher=Math.unl.edu |date=2010-11-18 |accessdate=2012-10-31}}</ref>

From 1997 until 2000, Wiegand was president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.unl.edu/sylvia-wiegand |title=Sylvia Wiegand's Homepage |publisher=Math.unl.edu |date= |accessdate=2012-10-31}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199901/awm.pdf|title=AWM Profile|publisher=Ams.org|accessdate=2012-10-31}}</ref>

Wiegand has been an editor for [[Communications in Algebra]] and the [[Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics]].<ref name="Sylvia Wiegand"/>  She was on the board of directors of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] from 1997 to 2000.<ref name="Sylvia Wiegand"/>

Wiegand was an [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Council member at large.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Wiegand is featured in the book ''Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary'', edited by Charlene Morrow and Teri Perl, published in 1998.<ref name="agnesscott1"/> For her work in improving the status of women in mathematics, she was awarded the University of Nebraska–Lincoln's Outstanding Contribution to the Status of Women Award in 2000.<ref name="autogenerated1"/> In May 2005, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln hosted the Nebraska Commutative Algebra Conference: WiegandFest "in celebration of the many important contributions of Sylvia and her husband Roger Wiegand."<ref name="agnesscott1"/>

In 2012, she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-09-01.</ref>

In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=9 January 2021}}</ref>
